**Gerald T. Whelan** (May 14, 1925 – January 2, 1993) was an American politician who served as the 30th lieutenant governor of Nebraska from 1975 to 1979.
Whelan was born in Hastings, Nebraska on May 14, 1925. He graduated from University of Nebraska–Lincoln, obtained a law degree from Creighton University, and practiced law in Hastings.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Whelan#cite_note-book1-1)
In 1960, Whelan won the Democratic nomination to run for [Nebraska's 1st congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska's_1st_congressional_district "Nebraska's 1st congressional district"), and lost to incumbent Republican Phillip Hart Weaver in the general election.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Whelan#cite_note-1960-1-2)
Whelan, with the endorsement of Democratic governor J. James Exon, beat longtime Nebraska politician Terry Carpenter in the Democratic primary in May 1974 for lieutenant governor, and went on to win the general election.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Whelan#cite_note-whelan1-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Whelan#cite_note-exon1-4) In the 1978 election, Whelan ran for Nebraska Governor, but lost to Charles Thone.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Whelan#cite_note-thone1-5)

Whelan married Virginia Kellison (1927–2010) in 1948 and had four children together.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Whelan#cite_note-virgobit-6)

**Hastings** is a city in and the county seat of Adams County, Nebraska, United States.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-GR6-3) The population was 25,152 at the 2020 census, making it the 8th most populous city in Nebraska.
Edwin Perkins invented Kool-Aid in Hastings in 1927; the town celebrates the invention with the Kool-Aid Days festival every August.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-5)
During World War II, Hastings operated the largest Naval Ammunition Depot in the United States, and for this reason was awarded the distinction of American World War II Heritage City by the National Park Service in 2023.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-6)

Hastings was founded in 1872 at the intersection of the Burlington and Missouri River Railroad and the St. Joseph and Denver City Railroad. It was named for Colonel D. T. Hastings of the St. Joseph and Grand Island Railroad, who was instrumental in building the railroad through Adams County.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-9) The area was previously open plain: the Donner Party passed through on its way to California in 1846 and a pioneer cemetery marker in Hastings bears an inscription taken from Tamsen Donner's journal: "The country between the Blue and the Platte is beautiful beyond compare. Never have I seen so varied a country so suitable to cultivation."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-spilinek-10):9 In the 1870s, railroads lured European immigrants to the new state of Nebraska with advertisements. Hastings' first settlers were English, from Liverpool, and were quickly joined by other English, Irish, Germans, Danes, and Germans from Russia, along with settlers from Midwestern and Northeastern states.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-spilinek-10):9

Between 1872 and 1880, when the population had grown to 2,800, Hastings was a boomtown. Settlers first built sod houses, dugouts, and shanties, then houses and stores. The city was incorporated in April 1874, and in September 1878, after a five-year county seat war, the county seat was transferred to Hastings from Juniata.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-11) However, a fire in 1879 destroyed 33 buildings downtown. The city was rebuilt between 1880 and 1890 in fireproof materials and in a more planned fashion, with characteristically ornate Victorian buildings, many designed by Charles C. Rittenhouse, the first practicing architect in Adams County and also mayor for ten years.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-architects-12) Thanks to the railroads, the city enjoyed great prosperity during the Gilded Age. The population grew to 13,500. This period of expansion ended with the drought and agricultural depression of the 1890s; the town's population fell to 7,000 and would not reach 15,000 until 1930.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-spilinek-10):9
African Americans have lived in Hastings since the 1860s. In 1876, Horace G. Newsom started the first Black-owned newspaper in Nebraska.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-13)

Hastings saw renewed growth from 1900 to 1930, which is reflected by buildings in the Craftsman, Prairie, Colonial Revival, and American Foursquare styles. The leading Arts and Crafts architect was Claude W. Way.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-architects-12) Hastings had four brickyards and in 1911 was producing more bricks than any other city in Nebraska,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-14) and all the paving bricks.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-villageprofile-15) During this period, the city also became known as the cigar-making capital of Nebraska. The largest cigar factory, the Kipp Cigar Company, was by 1921 hand-rolling one-fifth of all cigars produced in Nebraska; in 1925 it produced half, a total of 10 million.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-spilinek-10):72[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-16) Cigars lost their popularity to cigarettes between the two World Wars, and in the 1930s the Great Depression again brought the town's expansion to a halt._[citation needed_]

Hastings is the principal city of the Hastings, Nebraska Micropolitan Statistical Area, which consists of Adams and Clay counties.

As of the 2020 census, Hastings had a population of 25,152.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020DP-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020PL-30) There were 10,333 households and 6,139 families, and the population density was 1,691.5 per square mile (653.1/km 2).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020DP-29)
The median age was 36.7 years. 23.7% of residents were under the age of 18 and 18.2% were 65 years of age or older; 13.0% were between 18 and 24, 22.6% were from 25 to 44, and 22.8% were from 45 to 64. For every 100 females there were 95.9 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 94.5 males age 18 and over.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020DP-29)
98.6% of residents lived in urban areas, while 1.4% lived in rural areas.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020DHC-31)

Of the 10,333 households, 28.6% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 43.7% were married-couple households, 19.9% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 29.2% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 34.0% of all households were made up of individuals and 15.4% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020DP-29)
There were 11,279 housing units, of which 8.4% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.5% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.2%.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020DP-29)

**Adams County History**

Etymology: John Adams (2nd U.S. president)
Officially established on February 16, 1867, Adams County was named in honor of John Adams, the second president of the United States. Originally, Juniata was designated as the county seat. However, a rival settlement called Hastings began rapidly growing as a result of its burgeoning railroad infrastructure. A decade-long fight for the county seat quickly unfolded.
Juniata initially prevailed in the first county election in 1871. In response, Hastings residents held a meeting in 1873 where a special committee developed plans to locate the county seat in their community. Unwilling to surrender the county seat without a fight, Juniata residents adopted a resolution to build a courthouse in the community in 1874. The Adams County board began securing bids for the project’s construction.

However, the Adams County clerk at the time declined to provide the necessary paperwork to open the bids for the Juniata courthouse. After the County Board vacated his position for failing to fulfill his office, the clerk then refused to surrender the keys to the office. Additional complications arose in the form of a restraining order preventing construction at the planned courthouse site in Juniata. In 1877, Adams County residents voted again. This time, Hastings was chosen as the county seat. According to local history, Hastings residents retrieved the county records and transported them to Hastings under the cover of darkness to avoid provoking any further altercations.
In 1889, Adams County built its courthouse in Hastings. The building lasted until the present courthouse was dedicated in 1964.
Today, Adams County is part of an area of Nebraska known as the Tri-Cities. The county hosts two institutions of higher education--Hastings College and Central Community College--and has several hotels and a convention center.

**Hastings** is a city in and the county seat of Adams County, Nebraska, United States.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-GR6-3) The population was 25,152 at the 2020 census, making it the 8th most populous city in Nebraska.
Edwin Perkins invented Kool-Aid in Hastings in 1927; the town celebrates the invention with the Kool-Aid Days festival every August.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-5)
During World War II, Hastings operated the largest Naval Ammunition Depot in the United States, and for this reason was awarded the distinction of American World War II Heritage City by the National Park Service in 2023.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-6)
texts.2: Hastings was founded in 1872 at the intersection of the Burlington and Missouri River Railroad and the St. Joseph and Denver City Railroad. It was named for Colonel D. T. Hastings of the St. Joseph and Grand Island Railroad, who was instrumental in building the railroad through Adams County.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-9) The area was previously open plain: the Donner Party passed through on its way to California in 1846 and a pioneer cemetery marker in Hastings bears an inscription taken from Tamsen Donner's journal: "The country between the Blue and the Platte is beautiful beyond compare. Never have I seen so varied a country so suitable to cultivation."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-spilinek-10):9 In the 1870s, railroads lured European immigrants to the new state of Nebraska with advertisements. Hastings' first settlers were English, from Liverpool, and were quickly joined by other English, Irish, Germans, Danes, and Germans from Russia, along with settlers from Midwestern and Northeastern states.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-spilinek-10):9
texts.3:
Between 1872 and 1880, when the population had grown to 2,800, Hastings was a boomtown. Settlers first built sod houses, dugouts, and shanties, then houses and stores. The city was incorporated in April 1874, and in September 1878, after a five-year county seat war, the county seat was transferred to Hastings from Juniata.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-11) However, a fire in 1879 destroyed 33 buildings downtown. The city was rebuilt between 1880 and 1890 in fireproof materials and in a more planned fashion, with characteristically ornate Victorian buildings, many designed by Charles C. Rittenhouse, the first practicing architect in Adams County and also mayor for ten years.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-architects-12) Thanks to the railroads, the city enjoyed great prosperity during the Gilded Age. The population grew to 13,500. This period of expansion ended with the drought and agricultural depression of the 1890s; the town's population fell to 7,000 and would not reach 15,000 until 1930.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-spilinek-10):9
African Americans have lived in Hastings since the 1860s. In 1876, Horace G. Newsom started the first Black-owned newspaper in Nebraska.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-13)
texts.4:
Hastings saw renewed growth from 1900 to 1930, which is reflected by buildings in the Craftsman, Prairie, Colonial Revival, and American Foursquare styles. The leading Arts and Crafts architect was Claude W. Way.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-architects-12) Hastings had four brickyards and in 1911 was producing more bricks than any other city in Nebraska,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-14) and all the paving bricks.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-villageprofile-15) During this period, the city also became known as the cigar-making capital of Nebraska. The largest cigar factory, the Kipp Cigar Company, was by 1921 hand-rolling one-fifth of all cigars produced in Nebraska; in 1925 it produced half, a total of 10 million.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-spilinek-10):72[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-16) Cigars lost their popularity to cigarettes between the two World Wars, and in the 1930s the Great Depression again brought the town's expansion to a halt._[citation needed_]

As of the 2020 census, Hastings had a population of 25,152.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020DP-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020PL-30) There were 10,333 households and 6,139 families, and the population density was 1,691.5 per square mile (653.1/km 2).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020DP-29)
The median age was 36.7 years. 23.7% of residents were under the age of 18 and 18.2% were 65 years of age or older; 13.0% were between 18 and 24, 22.6% were from 25 to 44, and 22.8% were from 45 to 64. For every 100 females there were 95.9 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 94.5 males age 18 and over.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020DP-29)
98.6% of residents lived in urban areas, while 1.4% lived in rural areas.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020DHC-31)
texts.14:
Of the 10,333 households, 28.6% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 43.7% were married-couple households, 19.9% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 29.2% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 34.0% of all households were made up of individuals and 15.4% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020DP-29)
There were 11,279 housing units, of which 8.4% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.5% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.2%.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings,_Nebraska#cite_note-Census2020DP-29)

**Adams County History**
Number of Registered Historic Places: 22
Year Authorized: 1867
Year Organized: 1871
Etymology: John Adams (2nd U.S. president)
Officially established on February 16, 1867, Adams County was named in honor of John Adams, the second president of the United States. Originally, Juniata was designated as the county seat. However, a rival settlement called Hastings began rapidly growing as a result of its burgeoning railroad infrastructure. A decade-long fight for the county seat quickly unfolded.
Juniata initially prevailed in the first county election in 1871. In response, Hastings residents held a meeting in 1873 where a special committee developed plans to locate the county seat in their community. Unwilling to surrender the county seat without a fight, Juniata residents adopted a resolution to build a courthouse in the community in 1874. The Adams County board began securing bids for the project’s construction.

However, the Adams County clerk at the time declined to provide the necessary paperwork to open the bids for the Juniata courthouse. After the County Board vacated his position for failing to fulfill his office, the clerk then refused to surrender the keys to the office. Additional complications arose in the form of a restraining order preventing construction at the planned courthouse site in Juniata. In 1877, Adams County residents voted again. This time, Hastings was chosen as the county seat. According to local history, Hastings residents retrieved the county records and transported them to Hastings under the cover of darkness to avoid provoking any further altercations.
In 1889, Adams County built its courthouse in Hastings. The building lasted until the present courthouse was dedicated in 1964.
Today, Adams County is part of an area of Nebraska known as the Tri-Cities. The county hosts two institutions of higher education--Hastings College and Central Community College--and has several hotels and a convention center.
